analysis_purpose: Sampling-based optimisation under bounded uncertainty: use a scrambled Sobol low-discrepancy sequence to cover the joint uncertainty space, solve the deterministic industrial-symbiosis MILP independently at every realization, and report the empirical range of optimal decisions and outcomes. No Sobol sensitivity indices are calculated. The JSON uncertainty_range entries are authoritative for the stochastic/QMC run; OAT registry search ranges are not used as stochastic bounds.

terminology.recommended_thesis_name: Sobol quasi-Monte-Carlo solution-space assessment under parametric uncertainty
terminology.do_not_call: variance-based global sensitivity analysis unless actual Sobol indices are being estimated
terminology.not_two_stage_stochastic_programming: There is no scenario-independent first-stage design shared across all uncertainty realizations in this package. Each sampled realization is re-optimised independently.
terminology.sobol_meaning: Sobol refers to the low-discrepancy sampling sequence, not to Sobol sensitivity indices.
terminology.probability_warning: Triangular distributions use the live nominal value as mode and source-informed or explicitly assumed bounds. These are judgement-based epistemic measures, not empirically calibrated real-world probabilities.

parameter_selection_principles: Do not sample mathematically redundant global and polymer-specific multipliers for the same quantity in the same ensemble.
Use polymer-specific recovery and recyclate values because the decision problem is polymer-specific.
Use one total-plastic uncertainty plus a compositional closure block rather than independent polymer masses and independent shares.

Exclude route-outage and polymer-not-accepted ensembles from the final uncertainty run; prioritise recovery, composition, market, process and environmental uncertainty that directly affects the optimisation trade-offs.
Keep vehicle type endogenous: diesel vs battery-electric HGV is an optimiser decision to report, while payload and service cost are uncertain inputs.
Never sample payload above the loaded physical maximum; the previous +25% payload upper range was not physically defensible.

default_sampling.measure: triangular inverse-CDF marginals with live nominal modes and stated bounds
default_sampling.nested_power_of_two_design: A single 2^11 run is analysed retrospectively at prefixes 2^5, 2^6, ..., 2^11 for sample-size stability. No additional optimisation runs are needed for convergence assessment.

analysis.cppa_price_rule_note: Scale the 2026 nominal cPPA tariff by the same sampled DESNZ Reference delivered-price-path multiplier as the grid tariff; no independent premium is sampled.

convergence_reporting.central_regime_definition: The macro decision regime selected by the central deterministic MILP at nominal parameter values.
convergence_reporting.central_regime_share_definition: At each nested Sobol prefix, the number of feasible sampled realizations whose optimal macro regime exactly matches the central deterministic regime divided by the number of feasible realizations in that prefix.
stability_metrics: change from previous nested sample size (percentage points)
absolute difference from the final 2048-sample share (percentage points)
number of distinct macro regimes discovered
convergence_reporting.interpretation: Nested scrambled-Sobol diagnostics describe the declared triangular uncertainty measures; they are not iid binomial confidence intervals or empirically calibrated event probabilities.

bound_validation.zero_rule: Every selected continuous Sobol dimension must have a strictly positive lower bound. Zero is reserved for explicit outage/stress cases, which are excluded from this final run.
bound_validation.range_tier: plausible operating/market uncertainty; extreme boundary-search values remain in the separate OAT analysis
bound_validation.runner_behaviour: The runner fails before sampling if a selected positive continuous parameter resolves to a lower bound <= 0.

grid_electricity_price_multiplier.range_basis: The DESNZ EEP Annex M Reference annual delivered-price pathway in the electricity-decarbonisation module is divided by its 2026 value of GBP 182.71/MWh. Its 2026-2040 low is 2029 (GBP 164.131/MWh; multiplier 0.898317) and high is 2040 (GBP 185.698/MWh; multiplier 1.016352). Both grid and cPPA tariffs scale from their unchanged 2026 nominal values by the same sampled multiplier, preserving 2026 parity. This triangular time-path stress envelope is not a probability distribution for 2026 price uncertainty.

source_detail.source: DESNZ Energy and Emissions Projections 2024–2050, Annex M Reference annual delivered-price path in electricity_decarbonisation_simulation/outputs/annual_inputs_2026_2050.csv
source_detail.interpretation: Time-path envelope for the primary 2026-2040 study; not observed 2026 tariff variation. cPPA shares the multiplier and starts at its unchanged 2026 nominal tariff.

electricity_lcia_multiplier__grid__gwp.range_basis: 2026 NESO FES2025 ES1 pathway spread applied as a relative generation-mix change to the canonical ecoinvent GB medium-voltage grid factor. Holistic Transition is the nominal mode/lower endpoint (0.272552 kg CO2e/kWh); Falling Behind is the upper endpoint (0.358072 kg CO2e/kWh). The canonical high-voltage component is multiplied by each pathway's generation-score ratio to Holistic Transition, while its voltage bridge remains fixed. This is a conditional triangular sampling assumption, not a forecast probability or an absolute NESO grid LCA estimate.

source_detail.source: NESO FES2025 electricity supply data table ES1 v006; model technology LCA factor map and voltage bridge

autoclave_energy_demand.range_basis: Existing thesis low/central/high assumption: 0.2/0.8/1.4 kWh per kg plastic. This is one of the strongest directly evidenced modelling ranges.

total_plastic_waste_per_batch.range_basis: Lower: Reiners hybrid SUT 360 kg at 2,000 L, conservatively scaled to 1,000 L by treating half the mass as volume-sensitive (factor 0.75), then adding the reported 16% packaging and the current model mix-weighted defect factor 1.0222716635 once. Mode: current model 873.16823 kg/1,000 L batch, already including embedded packaging and defects. Upper: live model estimate plus a 10% buffer. Different SUT architectures and the partial scaling rule are epistemic envelope assumptions, not a measured 1,000 L distribution.

source_detail.source: Reiners et al. (2026), Figure 2 and Methods Model B; validated current SUT inventory
source_detail.double_counting_note: The central inventory includes packaging in assembly masses and explicit defects; packaging and defects are added only to the literature-derived lower bound.

manufacturing_throughput.range_basis: ±10% around the validated annual production plan. The runner applies throughput before the low/high-site allocation ratio so total throughput remains coherent; larger excursions are capacity stress scenarios.

low_to_high_batch_ratio.range_basis: Central allocation is 205/328 ≈ 0.625 in the validated model. The final QMC varies this ratio by ±20% (approximately 0.50–0.75 at the current central case), preserving a meaningful low/high production structure without sampling near-degenerate 0 or 1 allocation extremes.

utility_water_demand_per_batch.range_basis: ±25% around eligible non-contact utility-water demand. This retains meaningful process-water uncertainty while moving the earlier 50–150% exploratory interval to dedicated stress testing.

wastewater_generation_per_batch.range_basis: ±10% around process-model wastewater generation. Wider joint excursions with throughput and site allocation would primarily test installed WWT capacity rather than normal process uncertainty.

achievable_water_reuse_fraction.range_basis: 50–100% treated-water recovery. This spans materially degraded through full recovery while excluding zero/non-operation, which is a structural route-availability condition rather than continuous uncertainty.

recycling_capacity_fraction__mechanical_.range_basis: 75–125% of central contracted/operational route capacity. The interval represents throughput availability around normal operation; complete outage/zero capacity is deliberately excluded from the continuous QMC ensemble.

vehicle_payload__diesel_articulated_hgv.range_basis: Realised loading can be below the modelled maximum payload, but sampling above the vehicle maximum would be physically inconsistent. The previous +25% upper payload range is therefore removed. Payload is realised loading relative to rated maximum and therefore never exceeds the loaded maximum or approaches zero in normal operation.

vehicle_payload__battery_electric_articu.range_basis: Realised loading can be below the modelled maximum payload, but sampling above the vehicle maximum would be physically inconsistent. The previous +25% upper payload range is therefore removed. Payload is realised loading relative to rated maximum and therefore never exceeds the loaded maximum or approaches zero in normal operation.

transport_cost__diesel_articulated_hgv.range_basis: ±15% around the current all-in diesel HGV service rate.

transport_cost__battery_electric_articul.range_basis: 80–130% of the loaded BEV HGV service rate. The wider asymmetric range reflects less mature haulage pricing and charging/logistics assumptions without treating service non-availability as continuous cost uncertainty.

landfill_gate_fee.range_basis: ±10% around the loaded all-in landfill gate fee plus tax; larger policy-driven shifts are better treated as scenarios.

efw_gate_fee.range_basis: ±10% around the loaded EfW gate fee to represent normal market/site variability; larger shifts are scenario-level changes.

recycling_gate_fee.range_basis: ±20% around the mechanical-recycling handling proxy because pharmaceutical-plastic service pricing is less certain than landfill/EfW tariffs.

lifecycle_carbon_value.range_basis: Uses the thesis low/central/high structure: 0.5×/1.0×/1.5× the central lifecycle carbon value (approximately £132/£264/£396 per tCO2e when the loaded central value is £264/t).
lifecycle_carbon_value.interpretation_note: This is an uncertainty/stress range on an exogenous policy valuation, not a claim that the policy value is probabilistically distributed.

wastewater_treatment_annualised_capex.range_basis: 60–140% of the annualised wastewater-reuse CAPEX proxy because the estimate is scaled rather than a site-specific vendor quotation.

wastewater_treatment_opex.range_basis: 70–130% of the wastewater-treatment OPEX proxy to reflect chemicals, energy, maintenance and site-specific operation.

composition_weight__EVOH.label: SUT composition relative weight: EVOH
composition_weight__EVOH.range_basis: Relative composition weight varied from 0.80–1.20 around the loaded polymer mass; all polymer masses are subsequently renormalised so total sampled plastic mass closes exactly.
composition_weight__EVOH.interpretation_note: The sampled value is a relative compositional weight, not a direct mass fraction. The runner renormalises all six polymer masses to sum exactly to the sampled total plastic waste.

biomass_steam_efficiency.label: AD biomethane to useful external steam efficiency
biomass_steam_efficiency.range_basis: UK government Energy Technology List boiler briefing reports 80–96% net efficiency at full load for industrial steam boilers; the model’s 85% mode is the existing illustrative SEAI assumption. This is a transferred engineering range for biomethane-to-useful-steam conversion, not a measured efficiency for this residue or an offtake probability.
biomass_steam_efficiency.interpretation_note: Only the useful-steam displaced-service credit and useful heat quantity scale with efficiency. The AD/digestate inventory, gas-supply route, gas credit, feedstock mass, biomethane yield, RER steam activity and route costs remain fixed; absent a qualified external offtaker, this credit is conditional.

audit_notes.excluded_structural_stress_tests: Recycler outage and polymer-not-accepted stress ensembles are intentionally excluded from the final Sobol solution-space run. Computational effort is concentrated on joint uncertainty in recovery, polymer composition, process demand, route economics, transport, electricity, water and LCIA factors.
audit_notes.critical_range_resolution_fix: The final runner resolves all 48 registry-backed stochastic dimensions from this JSON uncertainty_range block around the live central value. Earlier drafts inadvertently retained the OAT registry low/high ranges for registry-backed parameters; those OAT ranges are not used by this version.
audit_notes.fixed_capacity_interpretation: Installed wastewater-treatment capacity remains fixed in the MILP. Therefore some joint combinations of throughput, batch allocation and wastewater generation can still be genuinely infeasible. Those cases are retained and visualised; the bounds have been narrowed so the QMC ensemble represents plausible uncertainty rather than an implicit severe capacity stress test.
